title: Complete Assyrian King List (All 116 Kings, Pruzsinszky), Remaining Sumerian King List Dynasties (Jacobsen AS 11) & Complete Babylonian Dynasties (L.W. King)

nodes.name: 1. Tudiya (1st Assyrian Tent-King)
nodes.role: First King of Assyria (Ebla Treaty Attested!)
nodes.notes: First of the '17 kings who lived in tents' in the Assyrian King List; historically attested in the Ebla archives concluding a trade treaty with Vizier Ibrium of Ebla!

nodes.name: 2. Adamu (2nd Assyrian Tent-King)
nodes.role: West Semitic/Assyrian Tent-King (Cognate of Adam!)
nodes.notes: Second king of Assyria in the AKL; earliest known historical ruler bearing the Semitic name Adamu ('Man/Red Earth'), cognate with Biblical Adam!

nodes.name: 3–8. Yangi, Suhlamu, Harharu, Mandaru, Imsu & Harsu
nodes.role: Assyrian Tent-Dwelling Patriarchal Kings
nodes.notes: Kings 3-8 of the AKL tent-dwellers, reflecting Amorite/West Semitic pastoral confederacies.

nodes.name: 9–10. Didanu (Tidnum) & Hanu (Hana)
nodes.role: Eponymous Amorite Tribal Ancestors (Cognate: Dedan?)
nodes.notes: Didanu corresponds to the Amorite tribe Tidnum/Ditanu (also ancestral to the Ugaritic royal cult and compared with Biblical Dedan); Hanu corresponds to the Middle Euphrates tribe of Hana.

nodes.name: 11–15. Zuabu, Nuabu, Abazu, Belu & Azarah
nodes.role: Late Tent-Dwelling Kings of Assyria
nodes.notes: Kings 11-15 of the canonical Assyrian King List (Pruzsinszky Table 17a).

nodes.name: 16. Ushpia (Builder of the Temple of Ashur)
nodes.role: Founder of the E-hursag-kurkurra Temple of Ashur
nodes.notes: Credited in inscriptions of Shalmaneser I and Esarhaddon as the earliest founder of the great Temple of the god Ashur in Assur.

nodes.name: 17. Apiashal (Son of Ushpia — Bridge to Ancestors)
nodes.role: Last Tent-King & First of the 10 Ancestors
nodes.notes: Appears at both the end of Section 1 (17 tent-dwellers) and the beginning of Section 2 (10 kings whose fathers are known), linking Shamshi-Adad I's pedigree back to Ushpia!

nodes.name: 18–24. Hale, Samani, Hayani, Ilu-Mer, Yakmesi, Yakmeni & Yazkur-El
nodes.role: Patrilineal Ancestors of Shamshi-Adad I
nodes.notes: Listed in reverse genealogical order ('PN1 son of PN2') in AKL Section 2 to trace the Amorite royal pedigree of Shamshi-Adad I (Pruzsinszky pp. 48, 51).

nodes.name: 25–26. Ilu-kabkabi & Aminu (Father & Brother of Shamshi-Adad I)
nodes.role: Amorite King of Ekallatum / Terqa
nodes.notes: Ilu-kabkabi fathered Aminu and the great conqueror Shamshi-Adad I.

nodes.name: 27–29. Sulili, Kikia & Akia (End of Ur III Period)
nodes.role: Early City-Rulers of Assur (Wall Builder Kikia)
nodes.notes: Kikia built the city wall of Assur; Sulili (son of Aminu) marks Assur's independence after Ur III.

nodes.name: 30–32. Puzur-Ashur I → Shalim-ahum → Ilushuma
nodes.role: Founders of the Old Assyrian Merchant Dynasty
nodes.notes: Ilushuma established free trade privileges for Akkadian merchants and founded the Old Assyrian trading empire.

nodes.name: 33–34. Erishum I (40 yrs, First Eponym List!) → Ikunum (15 yrs)
nodes.role: First King with Kültepe Eponym List (līmu) Chronology
nodes.notes: Erishum I rebuilt the Ashur Temple and inaugurated the Kültepe Eponym List (KEL), giving exact year-by-year dating from 1974/1934 BCE!

nodes.name: 35–38. Sargon I (40 yrs) → Puzur-Ashur II → Naram-Sin of Assur → Erishum II
nodes.role: Height of Old Assyrian Anatolian Colony Trade (Kanesh)
nodes.notes: Named after the great Akkadian kings Sargon & Naram-Sin; overthrown in 1808 BCE by Shamshi-Adad I.

nodes.name: 39–40. Shamshi-Adad I (33 yrs) → Ishme-Dagan I (40 yrs) & Yasmah-Adad
nodes.role: Founder of the Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia (Contemporary of Hammurabi!)
nodes.notes: Son of Ilu-kabkabi; conquered Assur, Mari, and Shubat-Enlil. His son Ishme-Dagan I ruled Ekallatum/Assur while Yasmah-Adad ruled Mari (famed in the Mari Letters!).

nodes.name: 41–47. Ashur-dugul & Six Usurpers (Ashur-apla-idi, Nasir-Sin, Sin-namir, Ipqi-Ishtar, Adad-salulu, Adasi)
nodes.role: Interregnum & Adasi (Progenitor of the 1,000-Year Adaside Dynasty!)
nodes.notes: Six 'sons of a nobody' ruled briefly; the last, Adasi, became the revered ancestor of Assyria's royal Adaside house down to Esarhaddon!

nodes.name: 48–53. Belu-bani (son of Adasi) → Libaya → Sharma-Adad I → Iptar-Sin → Bazaya → Lullaya
nodes.role: Early Adaside Kings of Assur
nodes.notes: Belu-bani (10 yrs) founded the unbroken Adaside royal dynasty; Bazaya ruled 28 years.

nodes.name: 54–66. Kidin-Ninua → Sharma-Adad II → Erishum III → Shamshi-Adad II → Ishme-Dagan II → Shamshi-Adad III → Ashur-nirari I → Puzur-Ashur III → Enlil-nasir I → Nur-ili → Ashur-shaduni → Ashur-rabi I → Ashur-nadin-ahhe I
nodes.role: Late Old Assyrian / Mitanni Vassalage Kings
nodes.notes: Preserved unbroken Adaside patrilineal continuity through the Mitanni era (Pruzsinszky Table 17b).

nodes.name: 67–72. Enlil-nasir II → Ashur-nirari II → Ashur-bel-nisheshu → Ashur-rim-nisheshu → Ashur-nadin-ahhe II → Eriba-Adad I
nodes.role: Transition to Middle Assyrian Independence
nodes.notes: Eriba-Adad I (27 yrs) broke Mitanni supremacy, setting the stage for his son Ashur-uballit I.

nodes.name: 73–76. Ashur-uballit I (Amarna Letters!) → Enlil-nirari → Arik-den-ili → Adad-nirari I
nodes.role: Founders of the Middle Assyrian Great Power
nodes.notes: Ashur-uballit I (36 yrs) wrote directly to Pharaoh Akhenaten as 'Great King' (EA 15-16) and married his daughter Muballitat-Sherua to Kassite Babylon! Adad-nirari I (32 yrs) annexed Hanigalbat (Mitanni).

nodes.name: 77–78. Shalmaneser I (30 yrs) → Tukulti-Ninurta I (37 yrs, Conqueror of Babylon)
nodes.role: Peak of the Middle Assyrian Empire
nodes.notes: Shalmaneser I founded Kalhu (Nimrud); Tukulti-Ninurta I captured Kassite King Kashtiliash IV of Babylon and built Kar-Tukulti-Ninurta — often compared with the Nimrod legend!

nodes.name: 79–86. Ashur-nadin-apli → Ashur-nirari III → Enlil-kudurri-usur → Ninurta-apil-Ekur → Ashur-dan I (46 yrs) → Ninurta-tukulti-Ashur → Mutakkil-Nusku → Ashur-resh-ishi I
nodes.role: Bronze Age Collapse Survival & Revival
nodes.notes: Ninurta-apil-Ekur (descendant of Eriba-Adad I) restored dynastic stability; Ashur-dan I ruled 46 years; Ashur-resh-ishi I defeated Nebuchadnezzar I of Babylon.

nodes.name: 87–97. Tiglath-Pileser I (39 yrs) → Ashared-apil-Ekur → Ashur-bel-kala → Eriba-Adad II → Shamshi-Adad IV → Ashurnasirpal I → Shalmaneser II → Ashur-nirari IV → Ashur-rabi II (41 yrs) → Ashur-resh-ishi II → Tiglath-Pileser II
nodes.role: Tiglath-Pileser I's Mediterranean Campaigns & Aramean Era
nodes.notes: Tiglath-Pileser I marched to the Mediterranean, hunted elephants in Syria, and compiled the Middle Assyrian Laws. Followed by 140 years of Aramean pressure until Ashur-dan II.

nodes.name: 98–101. Ashur-dan II → Adad-nirari II → Tukulti-Ninurta II → Ashurnasirpal II (Nimrud Palace)
nodes.role: Founders of the Neo-Assyrian Empire
nodes.notes: Adad-nirari II inaugurated the unbroken Eponym Canon (911-649 BCE); Ashurnasirpal II (25 yrs) built the magnificent Northwest Palace at Kalhu (Nimrud).

nodes.name: 102. Shalmaneser III (35 yrs — Black Obelisk of Jehu & Battle of Qarqar!)
nodes.role: First Assyrian King Explicitly Naming Israelite Kings Ahab & Jehu
nodes.notes: Fought King Ahab of Israel & Hadadezer of Damascus at Qarqar (853 BCE); his Black Obelisk depicts King Jehu of Israel ('son of Omri') bowing in tribute — the ONLY contemporary depiction of an Israelite king!

nodes.name: 103–104. Shamshi-Adad V & Queen Shammuramat (Semiramis!) → Adad-nirari III
nodes.role: Historical Queen Semiramis & Adad-nirari III (Tribute of Joash of Israel)
nodes.notes: Babylonian princess Shammuramat (Greek: Semiramis!) served as regent/queen mother alongside her son Adad-nirari III (28 yrs), who collected tribute from Jehoash of Israel and Ben-Hadad of Damascus.

nodes.name: 105–107. Shalmaneser IV → Ashur-dan III (763 BCE Bur-Sagale Solar Eclipse!) → Ashur-nirari V
nodes.role: Anchor of All Ancient Near Eastern Chronology (June 15, 763 BCE Eclipse)
nodes.notes: The Assyrian Eponym List records a total solar eclipse in Sivan under Ashur-dan III (June 15, 763 BCE), astronomically locking ALL Assyrian and Biblical monarchic dates!

nodes.name: 108–109. Tiglath-Pileser III (Pul, 745-727 BCE) → Shalmaneser V (726-722 BCE, Siege of Samaria)
nodes.role: Final Kings of Canonical AKL (SDAS Tablet) & Biblical 'Pul'
nodes.notes: Tiglath-Pileser III (called 'Pul' in 2 Kings 15:19) created the provincial empire; his son Shalmaneser V besieged Samaria (final king on the SDAS AKL tablet!).

nodes.name: 110–116. Sargonid Dynasty: Sargon II → Sennacherib → Esarhaddon → Ashurbanipal → Ashur-etil-ilani → Sin-shar-ishkun → Ashur-uballit II
nodes.role: Final Imperial Dynasty of Nineveh (Library of Ashurbanipal)
nodes.notes: Sargon II completed the conquest of Israel (722 BCE); Sennacherib besieged Hezekiah's Jerusalem (701 BCE); Esarhaddon conquered Egypt (671 BCE); Ashurbanipal built the great Library of Nineveh (preserving Gilgamesh!). Fell to Babylon & Media in 612-609 BCE.

nodes.name: Ur I Dynasty: Mesannepada → Aannepada → Meskiagnunna → Elulu → Balulu
nodes.era: c. 2560-2400 BCE (SKL Col. iii-iv, Jacobsen pp. 93-95)
nodes.role: First Dynasty of Ur (Royal Tombs of Ur Era)
nodes.notes: 5 kings (177 yrs): Mesannepada -> son Aannepada (restored from Tummal Chronicle & inscriptions!) -> Meskiagnunna -> Elulu -> Balulu.

nodes.name: Awan (3 Kings), Kish II (8 Kings: Susuda, Dadasig, Magalgalla, Kalbum, Tuge, Enbi-Ishtar, Lugalmu) & Hamazi (Hatanish)
nodes.era: c. 2500-2400 BCE (SKL Col. iv, Jacobsen pp. 95-99)
nodes.role: Early Dynastic Hegemonies of Elam, Kish & Zagros
nodes.notes: Awan (Elamite dynasty, 3 kings, 356 yrs), Kish II (8 kings incl. Kalbum son of Magalgalla), and Hamazi (King Hatanish, later deified in god-list AN:Anum!).

nodes.name: Uruk II (Enshakushanna, Lugal-kinishe-dudu, Lugal-kisal-si), Ur II (Kaku), Adab (Lugal-annemundu) & Mari (Ansud)
nodes.era: c. 2450-2350 BCE (SKL Col. iv-v, Jacobsen pp. 100-103)
nodes.role: Pre-Sargonic City-State Empires
nodes.notes: Enshakushanna of Uruk; Lugal-kinishe-dudu & son Lugal-kisal-si (ruled both Uruk II & Ur II!); Lugal-annemundu of Adab (90 yrs, legendary conqueror from Elam to Cedar Mountain); Ansud & 5 kings of Mari.

nodes.name: Queen Ku-Baba (Kish III — Sole Female Monarch in the Sumerian King List!)
nodes.era: c. 2400 BCE (SKL Col. v 36-41, Jacobsen pp. 104-105)
nodes.role: Tavern-Keeper Who Consolidated Kish & Founded Kish III–IV
nodes.notes: Ku(g)-Baba ('Baba-ellit', former alewife/barmaid, reigned 100 yrs) is the ONLY woman listed as sovereign king in the entire Sumerian King List; mother of Puzur-Sin & grandmother of Ur-Zababa!

nodes.name: Akshak (Unzi, Undalulu, Ur-ur, Puzur-Nirah, Ishu-il, Shu-Sin) & Kish IV (Puzur-Sin → Ur-Zababa → Simu-dar → Usi-watar → Eshtar-muti → Ishme-Shamash → Nannia)
nodes.era: c. 2400-2334 BCE (SKL Col. v-vi, Jacobsen pp. 106-111)
nodes.role: Dynasty of Ku-Baba's Descendants & Master of Young Sargon
nodes.notes: Ku-Baba's son Puzur-Sin -> son Ur-Zababa of Kish, whose royal cupbearer was Sargon of Akkad! Contemporary with Akshak's 6 kings.

nodes.name: Uruk III: Lugal-zagesi (25 yrs — First Unifier of Sumer Before Sargon)
nodes.era: c. 2359-2335 BCE (SKL Col. vi 24-27, Jacobsen pp. 110-111)
nodes.role: Ensi of Umma & Sole King of Uruk III
nodes.notes: United all of Sumer from the Lower Sea (Persian Gulf) to the Upper Sea (Mediterranean) before being defeated and led in a neck-stock to Nippur by Sargon of Akkad.

nodes.name: Late Akkad Interregnum (Igigi, Nanum, Imi, Elulu) → Dudu → Shu-Durul
nodes.era: c. 2193-2154 BCE (SKL Col. vii 1-12, Jacobsen pp. 114-115)
nodes.role: Final Rulers of the Sargonic Akkadian Empire
nodes.notes: 'Who was king? Who was not king?' Four rival claimants reigned 3 years before Dudu (21 yrs) and his son Shu-Durul (15 yrs) closed the Dynasty of Agade.

nodes.name: Uruk IV (Ur-nigin → Ur-gigir → Kudda → Puzur-ili → Ur-Utu), 21 Gutian Kings (Erridupizir to Tirigan) & Uruk V (Utu-hegal)
nodes.era: c. 2154-2112 BCE (SKL Col. vii-viii, Jacobsen pp. 114-123)
nodes.role: Gutian Domination & Sumerian Liberation by Utu-hegal
nodes.notes: 21 Gutian rulers from the Zagros mountains (Erridupizir, Imta, Inkishush, Sarlagab, Iarlagab, Hablum -> Puzur-Sin, Si'um, Tirigan [40 days]) expelled by Utu-hegal of Uruk V — whose general/relative Ur-Nammu founded Ur III!

nodes.name: Independent Lagash II: Ur-Nanshe → Eannatum (Stele of Vultures) → Urukagina → Gudea of Lagash
nodes.role: Sumerian Reformers & Statue-Builder Gudea
nodes.notes: Omitted from the partisan SKL: Ur-Nanshe, Eannatum, law-reformer Urukagina (oldest legal code against corruption), and pious Ensi Gudea of Lagash (contemporary of Ur-Nammu).

nodes.name: Isin I Dynasty (All 15 Kings): Ishbi-Erra → Shu-ilishu → Iddin-Dagan → Ishme-Dagan → Lipit-Ishtar → Ur-Ninurta → Bur-Sin → Lipit-Enlil → Erra-imitti → Enlil-bani → Zambia → Iter-pisha → Ur-dukuga → Sin-magir → Damiq-ilishu
nodes.era: c. 2017-1794 BCE (SKL Col. viii 23-45, Jacobsen pp. 124-127)
nodes.role: Final Dynasty of the Sumerian King List (Code of Lipit-Ishtar)
nodes.notes: Ishbi-Erra broke away from Ibbi-Sin of Ur III. Lipit-Ishtar issued the Sumerian Law Code (180 yrs before Hammurabi!). Gardener Enlil-bani succeeded Erra-imitti (substitute-king ritual!). Ended when Rim-Sin of Larsa conquered Damiq-ilishu.

nodes.name: Babylon I (All 11 Amorite Kings): Sumu-abum → Sumu-la-El → Sabium → Apil-Sin → Sin-muballit → Hammurabi → Samsu-iluna → Abi-eshuh → Ammi-ditana → Ammi-saduqa → Samsu-ditana
nodes.role: Complete Old Babylonian Amorite Dynasty (Venus Tablet of Ammi-saduqa!)
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: Sumu-abum (contemporary of Ilushuma of Assyria) -> Hammurabi (defeated Rim-Sin of Larsa, son of Kudur-Mabuk!) -> son Samsu-iluna -> Abi-eshuh -> Ammi-ditana -> Ammi-saduqa (astronomical Venus Tablet!) -> Samsu-ditana (overthrown by Hittite King Mursili I in 1595 BCE!).

nodes.name: Babylon II (First Sealand Dynasty, All 11 Kings): Iluma-ilu → Itti-ili-nibi → Damqi-ilishu → Ishkibal → Shushshi → Gulkishar → Peshgaldaramesh → Ayadaragalama → Akurduana → Melamkurkurra → Ea-gamil
nodes.role: Southern Marshland Dynasty Overlapping Babylon I & Kassites
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: Iluma-ilu fought Samsu-iluna & Abi-eshuh; Gulkishar anchored Babylonian chronology (696 yrs before Nebuchadnezzar I); last king Ea-gamil invaded Elam and was overthrown by Kassite Ulam-Buriash!

nodes.name: Babylon III (Kassite Dynasty, 576 yrs): Gandash → Agum I → Kashtiliash I → Agum II (Restored Marduk!) → Burna-Buriash I → Ulam-Buriash → Burna-Buriash II (Amarna Letters!) → Kurigalzu → Kudur-Enlil → Shagarakti-Shuriash → Meli-Shipak
nodes.role: Longest-Reigning Dynasty in Babylonian History (Zagros Mountain Origin)
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: Agum II (son of Urzigurumash) retrieved Marduk's statue from Hani; Ulam-Buriash conquered the Sealand; Burna-Buriash II corresponded with Akhenaten & married Ashur-uballit I's daughter!

nodes.name: Babylon IV (Isin II): Nebuchadnezzar I → Enlil-nadin-apli → Marduk-nadin-ahhe → Marduk-shapik-zeri → Adad-apla-iddina
nodes.role: Revival of Native Babylon & Recovery of Marduk from Elam
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: Nebuchadnezzar I sacked Susa in Elam and restored Marduk to Babylon; Adad-apla-iddina (Aramean/son of Itti-Marduk-balatu) married his daughter to Assyrian King Ashur-bel-kala.

nodes.name: Babylon V–IX: 2nd Sealand (Simbar-Shipak), Bazi Dynasty, Elamite Mar-biti-apla-usur, Nabu-mukin-apli, Nabonassar (747 BCE Era!) & Merodach-Baladan II
nodes.era: 1025-626 BCE (L.W. King Vol. I pp. 184-208; Eusebius)
nodes.role: Ptolemaic Astronomical Era of Nabonassar & Chaldean Resistance
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: King Nabonassar (747 BCE) inaugurated the famous Babylonian astronomical diaries & Ptolemy's Almagest Canon! Chaldean hero Merodach-Baladan II (Marduk-apla-iddina II) sent envoys to King Hezekiah of Judah (2 Kgs 20:12) against Assyria.

nodes.name: Babylon X (Neo-Babylonian / Chaldean Empire): Nabopolassar → Nebuchadnezzar II → Amel-Marduk (Evil-Merodach) → Neriglissar → Labashi-Marduk → Nabonidus & Crown Prince Belshazzar
nodes.role: Final Native Babylonian Empire (Hanging Gardens & Fall to Cyrus, 539 BCE)
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: Nabopolassar allied with Cyaxares of Media to destroy Nineveh (612 BCE); Nebuchadnezzar II built Babylon's Ishtar Gate & exiled Judah (586 BCE); Nabonidus (+ Queen Nitocris / Adad-guppi) & son Belshazzar fell to Cyrus the Great in 539 BCE!
